issues.description: Test change masks behavior: passing Addition(amount=0, puzzle_hash=zeros) instead of [] to avoid the new code path
issues.detail: The test diff changes additions=[] to additions=[Addition(amount=uint64(0), puzzle_hash=bytes32.zeros)] in two places. This is the smell of a test being bent to fit the implementation rather than the implementation being bent to fit reality. Either the old send_transaction/cat_spend semantics allowed empty additions and the new code path forbids them (regression — name it), or zero-amount additions to the zero puzzle hash now leak into real signed transactions (worse). Show me which. A test edit that exists only to placate __post_init__ is hostile to the next maintainer.

issues.description: cat_spend no longer forwards extra_conditions through cat_discrepancy path correctly — and silently drops puzzle_decorator
issues.detail: Old cat_spend passed cat_discrepancy via request.cat_discrepancy (computed property). New code passes extra_delta/tail_reveal/tail_solution into CreateSignedTransaction and lets it recompute. Fine in theory. But the new cat_spend call to create_signed_transaction omits puzzle_decorator entirely, while send_transaction passes it. If CATSpend ever supported a decorator (or grows one), this path silently drops it. State the contract explicitly or add an assertion that request has no decorator field. Drift between two adjacent endpoints is exactly the bug the refactor was supposed to eliminate.

issues.description: Discarded get_wallet return value with comment 'opportunity to raise' is bad taste
issues.detail: Calling self.service.wallet_state_manager.get_wallet(...) purely for its side effect of raising, then immediately discarding the return, then re-resolving the wallet inside create_signed_transaction — this is the special case that should be general. Either create_signed_transaction validates wallet_id (then delete the throwaway call), or extract a validate_wallet helper. The comment 'opportunity to raise' is the author admitting they know it smells. Don't ship code with apology comments; fix the shape.

issues.description: cat_discrepancy_validation duplicated as method on two classes instead of one shared base or mixin
issues.detail: The function was extracted from CATSpend.cat_discrepancy, then a verbatim-identical property was added to CreateSignedTransaction that calls it. Two classes now have the same property with the same three fields (extra_delta/tail_reveal/tail_solution). The duplication is now in the field declarations and the property wrapper, not the validation body. If you're going to factor, factor the whole thing: a CatDiscrepancyMixin with the three fields and the property. Otherwise next time someone adds a fourth field, they'll update one class and not the other.

issues.description: Three type: ignore[arg-type] in cat_discrepancy_validation papering over a real type problem
issues.detail: The comment 'Curious that mypy doesn't see the elif and know that none of these are None' is wrong — mypy doesn't narrow through 'None in {a, b, c}' because set membership isn't a type guard. The fix is to write 'if extra_delta is None or tail_reveal is None or tail_solution is None: raise ...' which mypy DOES narrow, and then the three type: ignore lines disappear. The current code lies to the type checker and asks the reader to trust the comment. Write the check in a form the type system understands.

issues.description: Patch does three things and should be three patches
issues.detail: (1) Extract cat_discrepancy_validation as shared helper. (2) Extend CreateSignedTransaction with CAT fields + puzzle_decorator. (3) Rewrite send_transaction and cat_spend to delegate. Each is independently reviewable; bundled they hide that the third changes user-observable validation (address-prefix check became ensure_valid_address; coin_announcements/puzzle_announcements/morph_bytes silently no-op for forwarded calls because callers don't pass them). Split it.

issues.description: Behavior change: send_transaction's error message and validation semantics changed
issues.detail: Old code raised ValueError('Unexpected Address Prefix') on bad prefix. New code calls ensure_valid_address(..., allowed_types={AddressType.XCH}, config=...) which has its own error text and may also reject addresses that the old prefix-only check accepted (or vice versa for testnet/mainnet edge cases). This is an API-observable change in an RPC endpoint. Either it's intentional (call it out in the commit message, update tests for the new error) or it's accidental (revert). Don't change RPC error contracts in a refactor PR.

issues.description: json_serialize_for_transport round-trip is the wrong shape for an internal call
issues.detail: send_transaction now builds a CreateSignedTransaction, calls .json_serialize_for_transport(...) to turn it into JSON, then hands that JSON to create_signed_transaction which presumably deserializes it back. Same process, same memory, two serializations and one deserialization for a function call. This is what the comment in the task description means by 'simpler and less powerful versions' becoming 'calls to' — but the right way is to call an internal _create_signed_transaction(request, action_scope, ...) that takes the typed object. The JSON round-trip is the special case that should be eliminated. Bad taste.

issues.description: Addition constructed with positional args; readability suffers
issues.detail: Addition(request.amount, decode_puzzle_hash(...), request.memos) uses positional args for a dataclass with optional fields. Three positional values where one is a list of strings (memos) and two are amount/hash — fine, but use keyword args. Streamable dataclasses tend to grow fields; positional construction breaks silently on field reorder.

issues.description: puzzle_decorator comment admits a hack in the type system
issues.detail: 'Technically this value was meant to support many types here / However, only one is supported right now and there are no plans to extend / So, as a slight hack, we'll specify that only Clawback is supported.' Either it's a hack and should be tracked with a TODO and an issue link, or it's the actual design and the comment should say 'Clawback is the only decorator; if we add more, widen the type.' Pick one. Apology comments without a follow-up issue rot.

review.summary: REFUSE in current shape; NEEDS-WORK to land. The direction is right — collapsing send_transaction and cat_spend into create_signed_transaction is the kind of special-case-elimination that's good taste. But the execution has three problems: (1) the test diff was edited to fit the implementation rather than the other way around, which hides a real semantics change around empty additions; (2) the patch does three independently-reviewable things and silently changes RPC error contracts (address validation) in the middle of a refactor; (3) the JSON round-trip via json_serialize_for_transport for an in-process call is bad taste — call the typed internal function. Fix the type narrowing to drop the three type: ignore lines, factor the duplicated CAT-discrepancy fields/property into a mixin, and split this into three commits. THREE-PATCHES.
